terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo stores a few searches in your trie and asks it for suggestions.

tasks.title: insert, has and startsWith
tasks.description:
Implement `insert`, `has` and `startsWith` on the `Trie` class in `src/trie.ts`. Words are lowercase letters `a` to `z`.

- `insert(word)` stores the word. Inserting it again adds 1 to its frequency (used in task 2). `insert('')` does nothing.
- `has(word)` is `true` only for a stored word, not for a prefix of one. `has('')` is `false`.
- `startsWith(prefix)` is `true` when some stored word starts with `prefix`. `startsWith('')` is `true` once any word is stored.

The check replays inserts and questions, including words that are prefixes of other words, an empty trie and the empty string.
nextSteps: Design a node: its children by letter, and what it needs to say about words ending there.
Write `insert` by walking down from the root, creating nodes as needed.
Write one helper that walks down a prefix and returns the node it reaches, or nothing.
Build `has` and `startsWith` on that helper and run `node src/demo.ts`.
hints: Each node needs a way to find its child for a letter quickly, and a marker for words that end at it.
Use a number instead of a boolean for the marker: how many times the word ending here was inserted. Zero means no word ends here.
`has` needs the node at the end of the word and a frequency above zero. `startsWith` only needs the node to exist, apart from the root of an empty trie.

tasks.title: Top completions
tasks.description:
Implement `topK(prefix, k)` on `Trie`.

- It returns at most `k` stored words that start with `prefix`. The prefix itself counts when it is a stored word.
- Words are ranked by frequency, highest first. Words with the same frequency are in plain string order (`a < b`).
- Fewer than `k` matches returns what there is. `k` of 0, or no match, returns `[]`. An empty prefix matches every word.
- Asking for suggestions does not change any frequency.

The check covers ranking, ties, the prefix as a word, small and large `k` and missing prefixes.
nextSteps: Find the node for the prefix with the helper from task 1.
Collect every word below it, with its frequency, by walking its children.
Sort by frequency, then by the word, and keep the first k.
Run the demo and read the second line.
hints: The words below a node are the node's own word, if any, plus the words below each child with that child's letter added.
A recursive walk that carries the text built so far collects them. Start it with the prefix, not with an empty string.
Sort with `(x, y) => y.frequency - x.frequency || (x.word < y.word ? -1 : 1)` and then `slice(0, k)`.

tasks.title: Delete and prune
tasks.description:
Implement `delete(word)` and the `nodeCount` getter on `Trie`.

- `delete(word)` removes the word completely, whatever its frequency, and returns `true`. For a word that is not stored, including a prefix of a stored word, it returns `false` and changes nothing.
- After a delete, every node that no longer leads to a stored word is removed.
- `nodeCount` is the number of nodes, counting the root. An empty trie has 1.

The check counts nodes after each delete. It also builds a trie of 150,000 generated words, runs 60,000 `has` and `startsWith` calls, 2,200 `topK` calls and 75,000 deletes, compares every answer with a correct trie, and expects it to finish in well under 2.5 seconds.
nextSteps: Keep a running count of nodes, updated when insert creates one.
In delete, walk down the word and remember every node on the way.
Clear the end-of-word mark, then walk back up removing nodes that are no longer needed.
Run the demo and read the third line.
hints: A node is still needed if a word ends at it or it has at least one child.
Removing a node means deleting it from its parent's children, so keep the path of nodes (and the letters) as you walk down.
Walk the path from the deepest node upwards. Stop at the first node that ends a word or still has children; every node below it can go, and each one lowers the count by 1.
